intro: Continence care is personal, skilled work — support the agreed plan with warmth and dignity, and report any change or concern promptly.
points: Never decide yourself that someone needs pads; a nurse or continence advisor assesses and prescribes the right products.
Treat continence care as skilled, dignified work — protect privacy, work gently, and never make someone feel a burden.
Encourage most adults to drink around 1.5 to 2 litres a day; drinking too little makes things worse.
Change wet or soiled products promptly and keep skin clean and dry to prevent soreness and pressure damage.
In older people, sudden new confusion with cloudy, strong-smelling urine can signal a UTI — report it promptly.
Report changes such as new leaking, constipation or sore skin; noticing and passing them on is your role.
